original_value: It is challenging to directly apply text classification models without much feature engineering on domain-specific use cases, and expect the state of art performance. Much more so when the number of classes is large. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN or Con-vNet) has attracted much in text mining due to its effectiveness in automatic feature extraction from text. In this paper, we compare traditional and deep learning approaches for automatic categorization of IT tickets in a real-world production ticketing system. Experimental results demonstrate the good potential of CNN models in our task.

result.paraphrase: Applying text classification models directly, without substantial feature engineering for domain-specific use cases, makes state-of-the-art performance difficult to achieve, especially when the class count is large. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs, or ConvNets) have drawn considerable attention in text mining because they can automatically extract features from text effectively. In this paper, we evaluate traditional methods alongside deep learning approaches for the automatic categorization of IT tickets in a real-world production ticketing system. Experimental results show that CNN models have strong potential for this task.
